the phenobarbetal (PB) inducers of cytochrome P450, P450b and 450e, are expressed in rat liver cells with a similar spatial distribution.

in situ hybridization techniques can be applied to the analysis of P450 gene expression, that P450b is expressed in a greater number of cells than P450e and that P450b mRNA accumulates to higher levels in the liver than P450e mRNA.
the phenobarbetal (PB) inductions of P450s, 1B1 and 1B2, are expressed in the liver in similar patterns and are not induced in the immediate periportal regions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the genes responsible for the expression of P450s in mammalian cells.
the development of in situ methods to assess the cellular distribution of specific P450s in liver and other tissues.

the expression and function of cytochrome P450 enzymes, a superfamily of heme-containing proteins that catalyze the oxidative metabolism of a wide variety of endogenous and exogenous chemicals in the body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of synthetic oligomers as probes for in-situ hybridization studies is a very useful technique for the analysis of P450 gene expression.
the expression of P450s in the liver and other tissues is complex and that a variety of factors influence the expression of individual forms.
in the liver, the P450s are expressed in a spatially heterogeneous manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the in situ hybridization technique using oligomer probes is a useful tool to determine the cellular distribution of mRNA and that this technique may be applied to the study of P450s in different tissues and in different chemical exposure conditions.
the in situ hybridization technique can be used to determine the spatial distribution of P450 mRNA within the hepatic lobules of rats and that the technique is sensitive and specific.
the expression of the PB-inducible rat P450 genes, P450b and -e, are regulated in a similar fashion and that their expression is restricted to a specific region of the liver lobule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in situ hybridization technique is a valuable tool for assessing the expression of specific genes.
we were able to show that the expression of two P450 enzymes, P450b and e, were expressed in a similar pattern within the rat liver lobule.
the expression of P450 genes is cell-specific and that this cell specificity is a major determinant of the cellular distribution of chemical toxicity.
